paths.description: Homepage and global navigation, representing the main discovery entry point.
Search results for “headphones”, representing listings, filters, and product discovery.
Headphones product detail, representing product information and the start of purchase.
Guest cart and empty-state recovery, representing basket state.
Invalid sign-in URL response, sampled as an HTTP/error recovery state.

findings.summary: The storefront ignores the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-preference retry screenshot shows the same white cards and light page surfaces as the standard capture; the platform probe reports colorScheme “normal”.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and retint surfaces, text, controls, and media-safe assets under prefers-color-scheme, following dark-mode guidance.

findings.summary: Menus use legacy custom positioning rather than semantic anchored overlays.
findings.evidence: The homepage exposes account/language disclosure controls, while the platform probe found 0 popover, 0 dialog, and 0 details elements and product DOM showed ordinary positioned boxes.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate transient menus to popover with CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks.

findings.summary: Dense navigation and merchandising chrome compete with the core content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile captures devote multiple stacked bars and a large carousel to navigation/promotions before product content; the search mobile view remains visually dense at tiny scale.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce repeated navigation and promotional chrome, prioritise search/results/product information, and progressively disclose secondary links.

findings.summary: Mobile receives a 1000 CSS-pixel desktop layout with horizontal overflow.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 viewport, layout measured scrollWidth 1000, visualViewportWidth 360, no viewport meta, and 640 px horizontal overflow. Product and search screenshots show the desktop page scaled down to illegible size.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid viewport meta tag and implement intrinsic responsive layouts that reflow to the visual viewport without fixed 1000 px assumptions.

findings.summary: Core components do not adapt at mobile/container widths.
findings.evidence: The same three-column product layout and desktop header are merely scaled down in the 360x800 product capture; DOM reports fixed 244 px buybox and 328 px feature column within a 1000 px page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container queries and intrinsic grid/flex sizing so header, gallery, buy box, and result cards recompose at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Several focusable disclosure targets are far below touch-target guidance.
findings.evidence: The focused-control probe measured language/account/fresh disclosure buttons at only 8x4 px; nav links are 30 px tall. Focus rings are generally visible, but the hit areas are too small.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand the actual button hit areas to at least 44x44 CSS px while preserving the visible focus treatment.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is poor and inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 7.1 s, LCP 9.0 s, Speed Index 9.7 s, and interactive at 21.4 s (performance 0.56). A separate trace measured LCP 2.64 s but 716 ms blocking time, showing substantial run variance.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, reduce render-blocking work, and validate field LCP/INP/CLS plus repeat lab runs.

findings.summary: A long main-thread task blocks responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded four long tasks, including one 742.46 ms task and 716.04 ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the responsible script in DevTools, split work into sub-50 ms tasks, defer non-critical initialization, and remove unnecessary execution.

findings.summary: The homepage has a heavy request graph and many render-blocking styles.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 274 requests and 2,982,341 transferred bytes. Its summary identifies at least five VeryHigh-priority parser-inserted stylesheets plus a parser-inserted challenge script; DOM confirms a classic stylesheet-heavy page.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles/scripts, consolidate dependencies, and explicitly prioritise only the LCP image.

findings.summary: Large scripts and cross-origin assets dominate delivery.
findings.evidence: HAR reports 1.45 MB of scripts, including a 590.8 KB WAF challenge and 474.3 KB vendor bundle; 270 of 274 requests are cross-origin relative to www.amazon.in.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit bundle coverage, conditionally load page-specific features, remove duplicate/legacy modules, and defer third-party/telemetry code.

findings.summary: Some controls have invalid or mismatched accessible semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.96 but failed aria-allowed-attr and label-content-name-mismatch; the image audit also found five images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct role/ARIA combinations, align accessible names with visible labels, and add empty or descriptive alt according to image purpose.

findings.summary: Heading structure is inconsistent across key templates.
findings.evidence: Homepage recon found no h1, while product discoverability reported eight h1 elements. Lighthouse also reported the accessibility tree is not well formed.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each template one clear primary h1, nest subsequent headings logically, and fix accessibility-tree semantics while retaining the good visible focus styles.

findings.summary: Zoom/reflow support is undermined by the missing viewport declaration and desktop-only layout.
findings.evidence: The platform probe reports no viewport meta; 360 px evidence has 640 px overflow and tiny scaled text/controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 without restricting zoom, then ensure 320–400% zoom and narrow reflow retain readable text and operable targets.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the errors-in-console audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate uncaught/runtime and resource errors, and add regression monitoring that fails builds on new console errors.

findings.summary: Image markup is poorly dimensioned and largely legacy-format.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 94/100 images without width/height, 62 without srcset, 99 legacy-format images, and 65 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Supply intrinsic dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes, modern formats where effective, and lazy-load non-critical below-fold images.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and DevTools issues remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed deprecations (one warning) and inspector-issues, and scored best practices 0.54.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API use, resolve DevTools Issues entries, and review BFCache/source-map/library diagnostics.

findings.summary: The homepage is not reliably crawlable and is not mobile friendly.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetched status 202 and found 0% raw/rendered word overlap, no raw title or description, and an apparent JS shell; Lighthouse also failed crawlable-anchors. Product detail did much better at 98%, showing a template inconsistency.
findings.suggestedFix: Return complete meaningful HTML and 200 status for the homepage to legitimate crawlers, replace javascript:void(0) navigation anchors with buttons or real hrefs, and add the viewport meta.

findings.summary: Homepage entity metadata is thin.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no JSON-LD and only two Open Graph tags on the public commerce homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite structured data and complete share-preview metadata, matching visible content.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence found five insecure cookies and auth-like session cookies without HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark sensitive cookies Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriately SameSite.

findings.summary: The page has a very broad cross-origin data and asset footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 13 third-party origins; HAR classified 270 requests and 2.78 MB as cross-origin, including analytics/ads endpoints, although many are Amazon-controlled and no built-in known-tracker match fired.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise telemetry, document purpose/retention, batch events, and load cross-origin services only when needed and consented.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The main document exposed none of the six inspected defensive headers, including frame protection, referrer and permissions policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors, strict Referrer-Policy and least-privilege Permissions-Policy; assess Trusted Types and origin isolation for XSS-sensitive account/checkout surfaces.

findings.summary: Asset delivery wastes bandwidth.
findings.evidence: Of 100 sampled images, 99 were legacy format, 62 lacked responsive sources, and 65 below-fold images were eager; HAR transferred 1.10 MB of images across 221 image requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where beneficial, provide responsive variants, reserve dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold merchandising imagery.

findings.summary: The homepage performs disproportionate background/network work.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 274 requests and the trace recorded 716 ms blocking time after load, with telemetry and many below-fold assets requested eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritise background fetches, batch analytics, and gate below-fold modules/assets behind visibility or interaction.

findings.summary: Cross-origin scripts and media consume most of the page budget.
findings.evidence: Cross-origin delivery accounts for 2.78 MB; scripts account for 1.45 MB and images 1.10 MB, with 13 third-party origins observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-template budgets, reduce cross-origin dependencies, self-host/cache critical assets where appropriate, and defer nonessential media.

findings.summary: Commerce capabilities are not exposed through a structured agent interface.
findings.evidence: The audited product/search/cart surfaces expose conventional HTML only; no manifest or structured agent capability was observed, and Lighthouse agentic browsing scored 0.50.
findings.suggestedFix: For selected safe commerce tasks, expose narrowly scoped WebMCP/agentic form tools with explicit user confirmation for consequential actions.

findings.summary: Route/state changes do not show evidence of View Transition integration.
findings.evidence: The platform supports document.startViewTransition, but the captured templates and DOM evidence show legacy full-page navigation and no transition treatment; the mobile/product captures show abrupt template changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance search-to-product and cart state changes with same- or cross-document View Transitions while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Rich disclosure UI does not use current semantic overlay primitives.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero dialog, popover, or details elements despite account, language, and navigation disclosure controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use button-triggered popover for transient menus and dialog only for modal tasks, relying on declarative light dismiss.

findings.summary: Large navigation chrome remains static rather than responding to scroll state.
findings.evidence: Homepage and product captures show two to three fixed navigation rows occupying the top of the content, with no observed scroll-state adaptation in DOM/CSS evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce or collapse secondary chrome after scroll using progressive scroll-state/container-query techniques with a stable fallback.

findings.summary: Modern phishing-resistant authentication was not evident in the sampled guest surfaces.
findings.evidence: No permission prompt appeared on load, but the account entry points lead to sign-in and no WebAuthn/passkey capability was observable in the inspected page evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys alongside recovery methods and request any browser permission only after a clear user gesture.

findings.summary: Text becomes too small to read comfortably on mobile.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 product and search captures show a 1000px desktop page scaled into the narrow viewport, producing very small product, price, filter and navigation text.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow rather than scale the layout; preserve at least 16 CSS px body text with comfortable line length and spacing.
